reason: Explains UCCL moving the transport control plane, including multipath, to software; secondary evidence for the CPU/software control-path design.
Describes CPU-thread transport callbacks, software CC, and a separate asynchronous control thread; usable evidence for UCCL host-side extensibility.
Identifies UCCL and software multipath on a streamlined existing NIC datapath; does not independently quantify flow-collision gains.
Directly explains RDMA reorder tracking memory and why random spraying overwhelms RNICs; supports the fine-grained-LB part, not the Jellyfish-specific result.
Explains RoCEv2 packet reordering misdetected as loss and the retransmission/state overhead of fine-grained balancing; partial support, not Jellyfish results.
RoCEv2/DDP traffic must stay within NIC reorder-buffer tolerance; directly supports the ordering constraint on packet-level balancing, not Jellyfish results.
An alternative relevant planner: network-aware grouping and automatic PP/DP/TP strategies consider heterogeneous GPU compute and memory capabilities; not Zorse-specific design evidence.
Explains the benefit of up-to-date per-packet feedback and states Spritz-Spray degrades with ACK coalescing; partial support for feedback/performance, not the buffer-inflation claim.
Explains common downstream paths causing sticky-flow collisions and motivates destination-based rotation; secondary same-family support for the structural imbalance.
Explicitly describes the earlier study as evaluating LB while decoupling congestion control and loss recovery; direct secondary summary of the requested work.
Supports the UCCL half of the comparison through its software control-plane description, not the PCM half.
